alternatives.root_cause: A runtime flag was flipped and the flagged code path in checkout fails, leaving the change log empty.
alternatives.why_not: A failing flagged path would surface as errors on checkout or its caller, but both error ratios stayed flat (tr_4366d707bbc2, tr_fa5bf545aadc); flag evaluations in pre-onset traces resolved in well under a millisecond.

alternatives.root_cause: checkout was cut off from the network and could no longer reach its dependencies.
alternatives.why_not: A partitioned but running process normally logs that it cannot reach anything; checkout wrote nothing at all (tr_d5b1c75e7de7), though the empty logs on unrelated services weaken this distinction.

alternatives.root_cause: A checkout dependency such as currency or payment became slow and checkout failed waiting on it.
alternatives.why_not: Every dependency span in the sampled traces completed in a few milliseconds (tr_417c48410a27) and cart showed a flat zero error ratio (tr_43f6b5655ee8); no dependency hop was the degrading one.

verdict.summary: The checkout process appears to have stopped doing work at onset while its socket still accepted: it emitted no telemetry after ~03:10 and no errors appeared anywhere in the call chain, so callers hang on PlaceOrder rather than receiving failures.
verdict.reasoning: checkout alerted first, yet its error ratio never departed from baseline (tr_4366d707bbc2) and neither did its caller frontend (tr_fa5bf545aadc), the edge proxy (tr_86a8a5ca8008) or its dependency cart (tr_43f6b5655ee8) - the incident is not an error-returning failure anywhere in the chain. All sampled checkout traces (tr_417c48410a27) predate onset and are healthy end to end, with every dependency responding in single-digit milliseconds, which rules out a slow dependency as the mechanism. Caller-side traces (tr_f7d0f76760e6, tr_5cb7f747a42e) likewise end before onset and contain no completed checkout path afterwards, the pattern expected when a callee stops responding and requests hang to their deadlines instead of completing. The change log for checkout was observed and holds nothing near onset - only an unrelated environment edit pair a day earlier (tr_6899666116e2) - so no artifact or config change explains it. checkout wrote nothing in the window (tr_d5b1c75e7de7), which fits a frozen process; a partitioned process would complain in its own log about being unable to reach anything. The main weakness is that log queries for frontend, frontend-proxy and product-catalog were also empty (tr_3f519e10ae76, tr_6e680a749256, tr_fcb4ae59e0cd), so the silence may be a collection gap rather than a signal.
open_questions: Whether checkout's log silence is specific to it or an environment-wide logging gap, since three other services were equally silent.
Whether any post-onset span exists showing a caller hanging on PlaceOrder to a deadline - no trace sample after 03:18:55 was returned at all.
Whether checkout's process was killed or stalled for exceeding a memory or CPU limit, which would make this resource_exhaustion; no host or container resource metric was examined.
Why checkout alerted at 03:20:46 when its own error-ratio series shows no sustained departure; the alerting condition itself was never inspected.
